# ledger_bank_connections (Data Source)

Lists Ledger's bank connections, oldest first, with their status, consent window and the freshness of each account. Read only, and needs an API token with the `connections:read` grant. The values are bank-sourced facts as Ledger reports them: they are never edited here, and they are kept apart from your own corrections. Reading changes nothing at the bank, and no consent is started, completed or refreshed (connecting a bank needs you at the bank's own page, in Ledger's UI). Account numbers, balances, provider session references and credentials are never read into Terraform state. The `as_of` and freshness values change as time passes, so a configuration that depends on them is re-evaluated on every plan.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Connections that need a new consent, and how fresh the data of each account is.
# Connecting a bank is done in Ledger's UI (consent happens at the bank); Terraform only reads.
data "ledger_bank_connections" "needing_attention" {
  status = "reconnect_required"
}

data "ledger_bank_connections" "all" {}

output "stale_or_failed_connections" {
  value = [for c in data.ledger_bank_connections.all.items : c.id if contains(["stale", "failed", "reconnect_required"], c.freshness)]
}

output "reconnect_needed" {
  value = [for c in data.ledger_bank_connections.needing_attention.items : "${c.institution.name} (${c.id})"]
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `status` (String) Only list connections with this status.

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) The connections. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `account_access` (String) `all` or `linked_only`.
- `accounts` (Attributes List) The accounts of the connection with their freshness. Balances, account numbers and identifier hints are deliberately not included. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--accounts))
- `application` (String) The name of the provider application the connection was made through.
- `as_of` (String) When Ledger computed the freshness (RFC 3339, UTC). Every plan reads it again, so a value that changes between plans is not drift in your configuration.
- `consent_expires_soon` (Boolean) An active consent ends within 14 days.
- `consent_granted_at` (String) When consent was granted (RFC 3339, UTC), or null.
- `consent_valid_until` (String) When the consent ends (RFC 3339, UTC), or null.
- `created_at` (String) When the connection was recorded (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `environment` (String) `production` or `sandbox`.
- `freshness` (String) The worst freshness among the accounts, or the connection's own state when it has none: `fresh`, `stale`, `failed`, `reconnect_required`, `disconnected` or `never_refreshed`. Stale or failed data is shown as such, never as current.
- `id` (String) The Ledger identifier of the connection.
- `institution` (Attributes) The bank. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--institution))
- `last_error` (Attributes) Why the connection last failed. Null when there was none. It carries the failure kind and the provider's code, never a bank payload. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--last_error))
- `last_refresh_run` (Attributes) The latest refresh run, or null when there was none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--last_refresh_run))
- `mode` (String) The provider's own mode terminology, `app` or `developer` (neither is production or sandbox).
- `needs_reconnect` (Boolean) True only when a new consent is the way forward (status `reconnect_required`). Never true for a retryable failure.
- `provider_name` (String) The banking-data provider.
- `refresh_available_at` (String) While in the future, a refresh on request is refused until this time (RFC 3339, UTC). Null when one is allowed now.
- `refresh_running` (Boolean) True while a refresh is going on in the background.
- `schedule` (Attributes) The background scheduler's view; null when background refresh is off or has not seen the connection yet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--schedule))
- `status` (String) `pending`, `active`, `reconnect_required`, `failed` or `disconnected`.
- `updated_at` (String) When it last changed (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `version` (Number) The object's version.

<a id="nestedatt--items--accounts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.accounts`

Read-Only:

- `currency` (String) ISO 4217 currency, or `XXX` when the bank reports the account in several currencies.
- `freshness` (Attributes) How current the account's data is. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--accounts--freshness))
- `id` (String) The Ledger identifier of the account.
- `name` (String) The account's name as the bank reports it.
- `no_longer_reported` (Boolean) The bank no longer reports the account.
- `product` (String) The bank's product name.
- `transactions_through` (String) The date (YYYY-MM-DD) transactions are held up to, or null.

<a id="nestedatt--items--accounts--freshness"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.accounts.freshness`

Read-Only:

- `last_attempt_at` (String) When a refresh was last tried (RFC 3339, UTC), or null.
- `last_error` (Attributes) Why the last attempt failed. Null when there was none. It carries the failure kind and the provider's code, never a bank payload. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--accounts--freshness--last_error))
- `last_success_at` (String) When the account last refreshed successfully (RFC 3339, UTC), or null.
- `notice_code` (String) A note about the last refresh, such as `transactions_rejected`, or null.
- `stale` (Boolean) Whether the data is older than Ledger's freshness threshold.
- `state` (String) `fresh`, `stale`, `failed`, `reconnect_required`, `disconnected` or `never_refreshed`.

<a id="nestedatt--items--accounts--freshness--last_error"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.accounts.freshness.last_error`

Read-Only:

- `code` (String) The provider's error code; may be empty.
- `kind` (String) `reconnect_required`, `rate_limited`, `retryable`, `permanent` or `canceled`. Only `reconnect_required` needs a new consent; `rate_limited` and `retryable` can be retried later.




<a id="nestedatt--items--institution"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.institution`

Read-Only:

- `country` (String) ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.
- `id` (String) The provider's identifier of the bank.
- `name` (String) The bank's name.


<a id="nestedatt--items--last_error"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.last_error`

Read-Only:

- `code` (String) The provider's error code; may be empty.
- `kind` (String) `reconnect_required`, `rate_limited`, `retryable`, `permanent` or `canceled`. Only `reconnect_required` needs a new consent; `rate_limited` and `retryable` can be retried later.


<a id="nestedatt--items--last_refresh_run"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.last_refresh_run`

Read-Only:

- `accounts_failed` (Number) How many accounts failed.
- `error` (Attributes) Why the run failed. Null when there was none. It carries the failure kind and the provider's code, never a bank payload. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--last_refresh_run--error))
- `finished_at` (String) When it finished (RFC 3339, UTC), or null while running.
- `id` (String) The run identifier.
- `outcome` (String) `running`, `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed` or `interrupted`.
- `started_at` (String) When it started (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `transactions_inserted` (Number) How many transactions the run added.
- `transactions_rejected` (Number) How many transactions Ledger rejected.

<a id="nestedatt--items--last_refresh_run--error"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.last_refresh_run.error`

Read-Only:

- `code` (String) The provider's error code; may be empty.
- `kind` (String) `reconnect_required`, `rate_limited`, `retryable`, `permanent` or `canceled`. Only `reconnect_required` needs a new consent; `rate_limited` and `retryable` can be retried later.



<a id="nestedatt--items--schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.schedule`

Read-Only:

- `consecutive_failures` (Number) How many refreshes in a row failed.
- `next_attempt_at` (String) The next attempt (RFC 3339, UTC), or null.
- `state` (String) `waiting`, `due`, `running`, `backoff`, `rate_limited`, `budget_exhausted`, `not_active` or `no_provider`.
